newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Local demand sparks rise of Russian pre-ADR shares.
newsitem.headline: Local demand sparks rise of Russian pre-ADR shares.

text.p: Shares in Russian companies with programmes for foreign investors to trade their shares abroad have outperformed the bullish Russian market, analysts say.
Observing this, Russian investors have snapped up the shares of firms thought likely to launch an American Depositary Receipt (ADR), the usual way to set up a foreign trading programme.

Salomon Brothers calculated that shares of companies with ADRs outperformed the Russian market by 37 percent in 1996 -- and the market itself rose 156 percent, according to the International Finance Corporation.

"Generally an ADR programme will have a positive effect on the stock price of underlying shares," said Rachel Canning, a research analyst at Renaissance Capital in Moscow. "But more so in the run-up to the launch."
In 1996, eight Russian companies launched the receipts, approved for trade by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission as U.S. securities representing foreign shares held by a depositary.
About 10 companies are expected to launch ADRs this year.
ADR programmes include privately placed tranches, level-one issues representing extant stock in a foreign company held by a depositary and level-three issues allowing issue of new equity.
"The reason for the price appreciation is simple," Canning said. "All of a sudden the stock is open to a wider investor base. And that investor base buys and will pull the price up."
Some major investors such as U.S. pension funds have rules which allow them to invest in emerging market shares only through ADRs.
But the companies that have issued ADRs are the top of Russia's low-liquidity, emerging market -- the choice picks in any case.
"An ADR in no way makes the company better," said Brunswick director of research Per Maelstrom. "It has to be a company that investors are interested in."

Maelstrom said that the stimulus shares receive from an ADR launch would wear off as the universe of ADRs grew and as the appreciation period was factored in closer to the announcement of plans for the ADR.
"You will see a lot less of (the post-launch ADR price rise) in the future," he said.
Three Russian banks also plan to issue ADRs, though their shares are practically not tradeable in Russia.

"Level one ADRs are more of a marketing tool for exposure in international markets for banks," said Danielle Downing, Emerging Markets Strategist at Salomon Brothers. "Level one ADRs add value only when there is a local market in the shares."
On January 1 this year shares in Russian ADR programmes represented 8.6 percent of Russia's total market capitalisation which was then $37 billion, Salomon Brothers said.
Downing said Russian market capitalisation was currently $54 billion after a New Year rally.
Downing wrote in a Salomon report that ADRs would track the market in 1997 but that shares in companies preparing to issue ADRs had the potential to outperform the market.
"By the end of this year you will have to be selective in which ADRs you choose," she said.
